item.subject: Mathematics
item.stem:
[Image: a scale in grams weighing three apples]

How much do the apples weigh in grams?
item.figure_description: A dial scale with three apples resting on the weighing platform at the top. The circular dial is labeled "grams" in the center. The scale is marked with numbers clockwise starting from 0 at the top, then 50, 100, 150, 200 (at the bottom), 250, 300, and 350. Between every two numbered intervals of 50 grams, there are tick marks dividing the interval into 5 equal subdivisions of 10 grams each. A pointer extends from the center and points directly to the second tick mark clockwise past 200.
item.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 fourth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
The graph shows the number of apples John picked each day.

each [Image: apple icon] stands for 10 apples

[Image: Pictograph of apples picked each day]

On which day did John pick 5 apples?
reference_items.figure_description:
A pictograph with a key stating: "each [apple icon] stands for 10 apples". A table contains four rows corresponding to days of the week:
- Monday: 7 full apple symbols and 1 half-apple symbol (right half).
- Tuesday: 5 full apple symbols.
- Wednesday: 1 full apple symbol.
- Thursday: 1 half-apple symbol (left half).
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (fourth-grade mathematics).

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: a stack of square boxes in the corner of a room.]

Ann stacks these boxes in the corner of the room. All the boxes are the same size.
How many boxes does she use?
reference_items.figure_description:
An isometric drawing shows a stack of identical cube-shaped boxes resting in the corner of a room. Three line segments represent the room's edges meeting at the corner behind the stack: a vertical line extends straight up from the top-back corner of the stack, a line extends down and to the left from the bottom-left of the stack along the floor, and a line extends to the right from the bottom-right of the stack along the floor.

The stack rests on the floor against both walls. The base layer is completely filled, measuring 3 cubes deep along the left wall and 4 cubes wide along the back wall (a 3 by 4 grid of cubes).

A second layer of cubes is stacked on top against the corner in a stepped pattern:
- Along the back wall (row 1, closest to the back wall), the first 3 columns from the left are 2 cubes high, and the 4th column is 1 cube high.
- In the middle row (row 2), the first 2 columns from the left are 2 cubes high, and the remaining 2 columns are 1 cube high.
- In the front row (row 3), the first column on the left is 2 cubes high, and the remaining 3 columns are 1 cube high.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 fourth-grade mathematics data.

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 fourth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.
